I am 53 years old, I went to primary school, and I have farmed this land for 35 years. My 7 mu is all wheat-maize double cropping, same as most families here in Quzhou County. I do not read books about farming. I learned from my father, from doing it myself, and from watching my neighbors. If Lao Wang or my cousin tries something new and their field looks good, then I might try it too. Otherwise I do what I did last year.

Right now it is spring, and my winter wheat is already in the ground since last October. I sowed improved wheat seed at 15 kg per mu. Before sowing I did rotary tillage and put down one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu as base. That bag is 15-15-15, so it has some of everything. Now at green-up I will spread another half bag of urea per mu — that is 25 kg. Urea is 46% nitrogen the dealer says, so that is strong. If the wheat looks a little yellow at jointing, I will add another 10 kg urea per mu. So total nitrogen for wheat is about 18 kg per mu. The compound bag gives me about 8 kg phosphorus and 7 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate four times: winter irrigation before the freeze, then at green-up after top dressing, then at jointing, and once more at grain filling. Diesel for the pump is expensive but I dare not skip. Last year my cousin skipped the jointing irrigation to save money and his yield dropped by nearly 100 jin per mu. I spray herbicide once after sowing, and if aphids or rust show up in spring I spray once or twice more. I expect 550 kg per mu if the weather does not turn bad.

For summer maize, after I harvest wheat in early June, I rotary till immediately and sow hybrid maize seed. Everyone around here uses hybrid now — my yield went up by a lot after I switched. I use 2.5 kg seed per mu. At sowing I put one 50 kg bag of compound fertilizer per mu. Then at the big trumpet stage I side-dress urea, about 15 kg per mu. Total nitrogen is about 16 kg per mu, phosphorus about 6 kg, potassium about 5 kg. I irrigate twice — at jointing and at grain filling — if the rain is not enough. The well gives good water but pumping costs money, so I watch the sky. I spray herbicide after emergence, and insecticide once for corn borer. Most years that is enough. I expect 650 kg per mu.

Fertilizer price went up again this year. I thought about using less, maybe cutting back half a bag. But then I remember 2015 when I tried to save money — the wheat was thin and the yield was terrible. A bad harvest is a disaster for my family of six. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost I can bear. So I will use the same amounts as last year. I will hire two workers for harvest time because my back is not what it used to be, but for spraying and fertilizing I do it myself.
